context: A city's library system lost about 28,000 visits this year, and the library board wants to know where to focus.
key_insight: Riverside accounts for almost all the drop: its visits fell 26,000 (60,000 to 34,000) of the 28,000 lost, while the other branches held steady

model_answer: Riverside explains almost all the drop: its visits fell from 60,000 to 34,000, 26,000 of the 28,000 lost, while the other branches held steady, so the board should focus there.

context: A mattress retailer started selling online in 2021 and is deciding whether to keep raising its online budget.
key_insight: online growth has stalled: sales grew $8M a year in 2022 and 2023 but only $1M in 2025, to $31M
chart_figures: Online grew $8M in 2022 (10 to 18) and $8M in 2023 (18 to 26); $4M in 2024 (26 to 30); $1M in 2025 (30 to 31), about 3%; Online sales tripled from $10M to $31M since 2021
model_answer: Online growth has stalled: sales rose $8M a year in 2022 and 2023 but only $1M in 2025, to $31M, so a bigger online budget may not pay back as it did.

context: A tutoring company's revenue has been flat at about $40M for three years. The CEO wants to know whether any customer group is growing.
series:
Primary school: 24 | 20 | 16
Secondary school: 12 | 12 | 12
Adult learners: 4 | 8 | 12
key_insight: adult learners are growing fast, tripling from $4M to $12M, while primary school fell $8M, which hides the growth in a flat total
chart_figures: Adult learners rose $8M (4 to 12), three times; Primary school fell $8M (24 to 16), 33%; Secondary school flat at $12M; Total flat at $40M; Adult learners' share rose from 10% to 30%
model_answer: Adult learners are the growth group: they tripled from $4M to $12M while primary school fell $8M, which is why the total looks flat at $40M.

context: A hospital's yearly surplus fell from $9M to $2M, and the board wants to know what to fix first.
categories: 2024 surplus | Patient revenue | Staff pay | Agency nurses | Supplies | 2025 surplus
key_insight: staffing drove the fall: staff pay and agency nurses together cost $11M, more than the $5M revenue gain
chart_figures: Staff pay −$6M; Agency nurses −$5M; Staffing together −$11M; Patient revenue +$5M; Supplies −$1M; Surplus fell $7M (9 to 2)
model_answer: Staffing drove the fall: staff pay and agency nurses added $11M of cost, more than the $5M revenue gain, so the board should start with staffing, especially the $5M on agency nurses.

context: A company that sells appointment-scheduling software to dental clinics wants to enter the European country with the most clinics that don't use such software yet.
categories: Country | Dental clinics | Share using scheduling software
key_insight: Italy has the most clinics without scheduling software, about 21,000, even though Germany has the most clinics

model_answer: Italy is the place to enter: about 21,000 of its 30,000 clinics don't use scheduling software yet, against about 12,000 each in Germany and Spain.

context: A pizza chain promises delivery within 30 minutes. It can add drivers at lunch or at dinner, and wants to know which comes first.
key_insight: dinner breaks the promise most: deliveries average 34 minutes at 6pm and 38 at 7pm, against 31 at the noon peak, so drivers should go to dinner first
chart_figures: 7pm: 38 minutes, 8 over the 30-minute promise; 6pm: 34 minutes, 4 over; 12pm: 31 minutes, 1 over; 1pm: 29 minutes; 8pm: 30 minutes
model_answer: Dinner is where the promise breaks: deliveries average 34 minutes at 6pm and 38 at 7pm, against 31 at noon, so the extra drivers should go to dinner first.
